2-5.title: Water's Magic Tricks!

en.title: Water's Magic Tricks!
en.welcome: Splash splash! Do you like water? Water is SO cool because it can do magic tricks! It can be wet and splashy, hard and cold, or floaty like a cloud! Let's discover water's amazing secret powers!
en.mainContent:
**Water you can drink!** When you're thirsty, you drink water from a cup. This water is wet and splashy! You can pour it, splash in it, and it makes puddles when it rains. Wet water is called a LIQUID. Can you say liquid? Lih-quid!

**Ice is frozen water!** What happens when water gets really, really cold? It turns into ICE! Ice is hard like a rock but it's still water doing a magic trick! Ice cubes make your drink cold. Snow and icicles are frozen water too! Frozen water is called a SOLID. Can you say solid? Sah-lid!

**Steam is water too!** When mommy or daddy boils water, do you see the white cloudy stuff floating up? That's STEAM! The water got so hot it floated away into the air! You can't grab steam because it's like a tiny invisible cloud. This floaty water is called a GAS. Can you say gas?

**The magic circle!** Water loves to change! Ice melts into water when it warms up. Water turns to steam when it gets hot. And steam turns back into water drops when it cools down - like the drops on your cold juice cup! Water goes around and around, changing all the time!

**Water is everywhere!** Clouds are made of tiny water drops. Rain comes from clouds. Puddles dry up and go back to the sky. Water is always moving and changing all around us!
keyPoints: Liquid water is wet and splashy
Ice is frozen water - hard and cold
Steam is hot water floating in the air
Water changes between all three forms
Water is everywhere - in cups, clouds, and ice cubes!
interactionPrompts: Can you show me how ice feels?
What happens to ice cream outside?
Where do puddles go when they dry up?
en.wisdomMoment: Water is like a shape-shifter! It can be wet, frozen, or floaty - but it's always the same water just wearing different costumes!
en.core_metaphor: Water is a magical shape-shifter that wears different costumes
en.cta: Go find some ice and watch it melt - you're seeing water's magic trick!
en.summary: You learned that water can be liquid (wet), solid (ice), or gas (steam) - and it changes between them like magic!

es.title: ¡Los trucos mágicos del agua!

**¡El hielo es agua congelada!** ¿Qué pasa cuando el agua se pone muy, muy fría? ¡Se convierte en HIELO! El agua congelada se llama SÓLIDO.

**¡El vapor también es agua!** Cuando el agua hierve, ¿ves esa cosa blanca flotando? ¡Eso es VAPOR! El agua flotante se llama GAS.

**¡El círculo mágico!** ¡Al agua le encanta cambiar! El hielo se derrite. El agua se convierte en vapor. ¡Y el vapor vuelve a ser gotitas de agua!

El hielo es agua congelada

El agua cambia entre las tres formas

6-12.title: Water: The Shape-Shifting Molecule
6-12.description: Explore the science behind water's amazing transformations

en.title: Water: The Shape-Shifting Molecule
en.welcome: Hey science explorer! Did you know that the water in your glass right now could have been a dinosaur's drink, a cloud in the sky, or frozen in an iceberg? Water never gets used up - it just keeps changing forms! Let's unlock the secrets of H2O!
en.mainContent:
**The Three States of Matter:** Everything around us is made of tiny particles called molecules. Water molecules are always moving, but HOW they move determines what form water takes!

**Liquid Water - The Flowing State:** When you pour a glass of water, the molecules are sliding past each other like a crowd of people walking. They stick together loosely, which is why water takes the shape of whatever container holds it. Liquid water exists between 0°C and 100°C (32°F to 212°F).

**Solid Ice - The Frozen State:** When water gets cold enough (0°C/32°F), something amazing happens! The molecules slow down and lock into a crystal pattern. They form a rigid structure that's actually LESS dense than liquid water - that's why ice floats! The molecules vibrate in place but can't move around.

**Water Vapor - The Gas State:** Heat water to 100°C (212°F) and the molecules get so energized they break free and zoom around as an invisible gas! You can't see pure water vapor, but when it cools slightly it forms visible steam or mist. Water vapor is all around us in the air - that's humidity!

**The Water Cycle:** Nature runs the world's biggest recycling system! The Sun heats oceans and lakes, causing evaporation. Water vapor rises, cools, and forms clouds through condensation. Clouds release precipitation as rain, snow, or hail. Water flows back to oceans through rivers, and the cycle continues forever!

**Phase Changes:** Melting (solid→liquid), Freezing (liquid→solid), Evaporation (liquid→gas), Condensation (gas→liquid), Sublimation (solid→gas, like dry ice!), and Deposition (gas→solid, like frost forming).
keyPoints: Water exists as solid (ice), liquid (water), or gas (vapor)
Temperature determines which state water is in
Water molecules move fastest as gas, slowest as solid
Ice is less dense than liquid water, so it floats
The water cycle recycles Earth's water endlessly
interactionPrompts: Why does ice float instead of sink?

en.wisdomMoment: The water you drink today has been around for billions of years, cycling through oceans, clouds, rivers, and living things. You're connected to every raindrop that ever fell!
en.core_metaphor: Water molecules are like tiny dancers that change their dance based on temperature

en.cta: Breathe on a cold window and watch condensation appear - you just made water from air!
en.summary: You discovered how water transforms between solid, liquid, and gas states, and how the water cycle keeps water moving around our planet forever!

es.title: Agua: La Molécula Cambiante
es.welcome: ¡Hola explorador científico! ¿Sabías que el agua en tu vaso podría haber sido la bebida de un dinosaurio, una nube en el cielo, o estar congelada en un iceberg? ¡El agua nunca se acaba - solo sigue cambiando de forma!
es.mainContent:
**Los Tres Estados de la Materia:** Todo está hecho de partículas diminutas llamadas moléculas. ¡Las moléculas de agua siempre se mueven, pero CÓMO se mueven determina qué forma toma el agua!

**Agua Líquida:** Las moléculas se deslizan entre sí. El agua líquida existe entre 0°C y 100°C.

**Hielo Sólido:** A 0°C, las moléculas se bloquean en un patrón cristalino. ¡Por eso el hielo flota!

**Vapor de Agua:** A 100°C, las moléculas se liberan y vuelan como un gas invisible.

**El Ciclo del Agua:** ¡La naturaleza ejecuta el sistema de reciclaje más grande del mundo! Evaporación, condensación, precipitación - ¡y el ciclo continúa para siempre!
keyPoints: El agua existe como sólido, líquido o gas
La temperatura determina el estado del agua
Las moléculas se mueven más rápido como gas
El hielo flota porque es menos denso
interactionPrompts: ¿Por qué flota el hielo?
¿Qué le pasa a un charco en un día caluroso?
es.wisdomMoment: El agua que bebes hoy ha existido por miles de millones de años, ciclando a través de océanos, nubes y seres vivos. ¡Estás conectado con cada gota de lluvia!
es.core_metaphor: Las moléculas de agua son como pequeñas bailarinas que cambian su baile según la temperatura
es.cta: ¡Sopla en una ventana fría y mira aparecer la condensación!
es.summary: ¡Descubriste cómo el agua se transforma entre estados sólido, líquido y gaseoso!

13-17.title: H2O: The Chemistry of Transformation
13-17.description: Dive into the molecular science behind water's unique properties

en.title: H2O: The Chemistry of Transformation
en.welcome: Water is so common we barely notice it, yet it's one of the weirdest substances in the universe. Its strange properties are why life exists on Earth. Let's get into the molecular chemistry that makes water the most important molecule on our planet.
en.mainContent:
**The Molecular Structure:** Water (H2O) has a bent molecular structure with oxygen at the center and two hydrogen atoms at a 104.5° angle. This seemingly simple arrangement creates a polar molecule - oxygen pulls electrons toward itself, creating a slightly negative end and slightly positive hydrogen ends.

**Hydrogen Bonding - The Secret Weapon:** Those polar charges let water molecules 'stick' to each other through hydrogen bonds. Each water molecule can form up to four hydrogen bonds with neighbors. These bonds are weak individually but incredibly strong collectively - they're why water has such unusual properties.

**Anomalous Density:** Most substances are densest as solids. Water? Maximum density occurs at 4°C as a liquid. When water freezes, the hydrogen bonds lock molecules into a crystalline lattice with MORE space between them. Ice is less dense than liquid water - that's why ice floats and lakes freeze from the top down, protecting aquatic life below.

**High Specific Heat:** Water resists temperature change. It takes 4.18 joules to raise 1 gram of water by 1°C - way more than most substances. This is why oceans moderate coastal climates and why your body temperature stays stable despite environmental changes.

**Phase Transitions & Energy:** Phase changes involve latent heat - energy absorbed or released without temperature change. Melting ice at 0°C requires 334 J/g (heat of fusion). Boiling water at 100°C needs 2260 J/g (heat of vaporization). This is why sweating cools you - evaporating water absorbs massive energy from your skin.

**Surface Tension:** Hydrogen bonds at the surface create a 'skin' strong enough for insects to walk on. This same property drives capillary action - how water climbs up plant stems against gravity.

**Universal Solvent:** Water's polarity lets it dissolve more substances than any other liquid. Salt, sugar, gases - water pulls ionic and polar molecules apart. This makes water essential for biochemistry; every chemical reaction in your cells happens in water.
keyPoints: Water's bent molecular shape (104.5°) creates polarity
Hydrogen bonds give water its unique properties
Ice floats because of its less-dense crystal structure
High specific heat moderates temperatures globally
Water is the 'universal solvent' essential for life
interactionPrompts: Why would life on Earth be impossible if ice sank instead of floated?
How does sweating actually cool your body down?
Why can some insects walk on water?
en.wisdomMoment: Water's 'weirdness' - floating ice, high heat capacity, universal solvent properties - isn't a bug, it's a feature. Every 'anomaly' of water is precisely why life can exist. The molecule that seems so ordinary is actually extraordinarily rare in the universe.
en.core_metaphor: Water is life's operating system - weird by design, essential by necessity
en.cta: Calculate how much energy it takes to melt an ice cube, then boil the resulting water. The numbers will surprise you!
en.summary: You've explored water's molecular structure, hydrogen bonding, and anomalous properties that make it the essential molecule for life on Earth.

es.title: H2O: La Química de la Transformación
es.welcome: El agua es tan común que apenas la notamos, pero es una de las sustancias más extrañas del universo. Sus propiedades raras son la razón por la que existe la vida en la Tierra.
es.mainContent:
**Estructura Molecular:** El agua (H2O) tiene una estructura molecular doblada con oxígeno en el centro y dos átomos de hidrógeno en un ángulo de 104.5°. Esto crea una molécula polar.

**Enlace de Hidrógeno:** Las cargas polares permiten que las moléculas de agua se 'peguen' entre sí. Cada molécula puede formar hasta cuatro enlaces de hidrógeno.

**Densidad Anómala:** El hielo es menos denso que el agua líquida - por eso flota.

**Alto Calor Específico:** El agua resiste el cambio de temperatura, moderando climas costeros.

**Transiciones de Fase:** Los cambios de fase involucran calor latente - energía absorbida sin cambio de temperatura.

**Solvente Universal:** La polaridad del agua le permite disolver más sustancias que cualquier otro líquido.
keyPoints: La forma molecular crea polaridad
Los enlaces de hidrógeno dan propiedades únicas
El hielo flota por su estructura cristalina
El alto calor específico modera temperaturas
interactionPrompts: ¿Por qué sería imposible la vida si el hielo se hundiera?
¿Cómo te enfría el sudor?
es.wisdomMoment: La 'rareza' del agua no es un error, es una característica. Cada anomalía es precisamente por qué puede existir la vida.
es.core_metaphor: El agua es el sistema operativo de la vida
es.cta: ¡Calcula cuánta energía se necesita para derretir un cubo de hielo!
es.summary: Exploraste la estructura molecular del agua y sus propiedades anómalas que la hacen esencial para la vida.

fr.title: H2O: La Chimie de la Transformation
fr.welcome: L'eau est si commune qu'on la remarque à peine, pourtant c'est l'une des substances les plus étranges de l'univers. Ses propriétés bizarres sont la raison pour laquelle la vie existe sur Terre.
fr.mainContent:
**Structure Moléculaire:** L'eau (H2O) a une structure moléculaire courbée avec l'oxygène au centre et deux atomes d'hydrogène à un angle de 104,5°. Cela crée une molécule polaire.

**Liaison Hydrogène:** Les charges polaires permettent aux molécules d'eau de 'coller' ensemble. Chaque molécule peut former jusqu'à quatre liaisons hydrogène.

**Densité Anormale:** La glace est moins dense que l'eau liquide - c'est pourquoi elle flotte.

**Haute Capacité Thermique:** L'eau résiste au changement de température, modérant les climats côtiers.

**Transitions de Phase:** Les changements de phase impliquent de la chaleur latente.

**Solvant Universel:** La polarité de l'eau lui permet de dissoudre plus de substances que tout autre liquide.
keyPoints: La forme moléculaire crée la polarité
Les liaisons hydrogène donnent des propriétés uniques
La glace flotte grâce à sa structure cristalline
La haute capacité thermique modère les températures
interactionPrompts: Pourquoi la vie serait-elle impossible si la glace coulait?
Comment la transpiration te refroidit-elle?
fr.wisdomMoment: La 'bizarrerie' de l'eau n'est pas un bug, c'est une fonctionnalité. Chaque anomalie est précisément pourquoi la vie peut exister.
fr.core_metaphor: L'eau est le système d'exploitation de la vie

18-35.title: Water Systems: Engineering Life and Civilization
18-35.description: How water's properties shape technology, infrastructure, and sustainability

en.title: Water Systems: Engineering Life and Civilization
en.welcome: Every civilization in history rose near water. Every technology we've built must account for water's behavior. From hydroelectric dams to HVAC systems to the biochemistry of our cells, water's phase transitions are the foundation of how we engineer the world.
en.mainContent:
**Thermodynamic Engineering:** Water's high latent heat of vaporization (2260 kJ/kg) is exploited everywhere. Steam turbines generate 80% of global electricity - water boils, expands 1600x, spins turbines, condenses, and cycles again. Refrigeration reverses this: compressing refrigerant releases heat outside, expansion absorbs heat inside. Your AC is a phase-transition machine.

**Infrastructure Challenges:** Water expands 9% when freezing. This cracks pipes, breaks roads, and shapes architecture. Northern cities spend billions on freeze-thaw damage. Smart engineering uses expansion joints, insulation, and controlled heating. Understanding water's volumetric behavior is fundamental to civil engineering.

**Climate Systems:** Ocean currents distribute heat globally because water's specific heat is 4x higher than air. The Gulf Stream carries tropical warmth to Europe. El Niño patterns demonstrate how slight water temperature changes cascade into global weather shifts. Water's thermal inertia stabilizes climate - and makes climate change effects lag for decades.

**Biological Systems:** Your body is 60% water. Phase transitions regulate you: sweating cools through evaporation, blood transports heat via convection, proteins fold in water's hydrogen-bonded matrix. Cellular chemistry only works in liquid water. Dehydration doesn't just make you thirsty - it disrupts every biochemical reaction.

**Water Scarcity Engineering:** Desalination (reverse osmosis, thermal distillation) converts seawater to freshwater but requires massive energy. Water recycling, atmospheric water generation, and fog harvesting represent emerging solutions. The water-energy nexus will define 21st-century infrastructure.

**Phase Change Materials (PCMs):** We're engineering substances that use water's phase-change principles for energy storage. Ice storage systems cool buildings during off-peak hours. Thermal batteries store heat in salt hydrates. The phase transition that made life possible is now enabling sustainable technology.
keyPoints: Steam turbines power 80% of global electricity via water's phase changes
Water's 9% expansion when freezing drives infrastructure design
Ocean heat capacity stabilizes global climate systems
Your body uses water's phase properties for temperature regulation
Desalination and water recycling are critical future technologies

en.wisdomMoment: Every glass of water you drink was engineered to reach you through systems that leverage the same phase-transition physics that powers cities and regulates your body temperature. The molecule that fills your cells also fills the pipes, turbines, and clouds that civilization depends on.
en.core_metaphor: Water's phase transitions are civilization's operating system

es.title: Sistemas de Agua: Ingeniería de la Vida y la Civilización
es.welcome: Cada civilización surgió cerca del agua. Cada tecnología debe considerar el comportamiento del agua. Desde represas hasta sistemas de aire acondicionado hasta la bioquímica de nuestras células.
es.mainContent:
**Ingeniería Termodinámica:** El alto calor latente del agua se aprovecha en todas partes. Las turbinas de vapor generan el 80% de la electricidad global.

**Desafíos de Infraestructura:** El agua se expande 9% al congelarse. Esto rompe tuberías y carreteras.

**Sistemas Climáticos:** Las corrientes oceánicas distribuyen calor globalmente porque el calor específico del agua es 4x mayor que el aire.

**Sistemas Biológicos:** Tu cuerpo es 60% agua. Las transiciones de fase te regulan: el sudor enfría a través de la evaporación.

**Ingeniería de Escasez:** La desalinización convierte agua de mar en agua dulce pero requiere energía masiva.
keyPoints: Las turbinas de vapor alimentan el 80% de la electricidad
La expansión del 9% del agua impulsa el diseño de infraestructura
La capacidad térmica del océano estabiliza el clima
Tu cuerpo usa las propiedades de fase del agua

es.wisdomMoment: Cada vaso de agua fue diseñado para llegar a ti a través de sistemas que aprovechan la misma física que alimenta ciudades y regula tu temperatura corporal.
es.core_metaphor: Las transiciones de fase del agua son el sistema operativo de la civilización

es.summary: Conectaste las propiedades termodinámicas del agua con los sistemas de ingeniería que alimentan la civilización.

36-60.title: Water Wisdom: Cycles of Change
36-60.description: Life lessons from water's eternal transformation

en.title: Water Wisdom: Cycles of Change
en.welcome: We're at a stage of life where we've seen things cycle - careers, relationships, seasons. Water has been cycling for 4.5 billion years, teaching a masterclass in transformation without loss of essence. What can this ancient molecule teach us about navigating change?
en.mainContent:
**The Paradox of Constancy Through Change:** Water molecules in your body today were once rain falling on dinosaurs, glaciers in ice ages, tears of ancestors. Water never loses itself - it just changes form. The same molecules flow through countless transformations yet remain H2O. There's profound wisdom here: identity doesn't require stasis.

**Adapting to Containers:** Liquid water takes the shape of whatever holds it without complaint. Ice holds firm structure when needed. Vapor expands to fill any space. Water demonstrates that adapting to circumstances isn't weakness - it's intelligence. The question isn't 'who am I?' but 'what form does this situation need?'

**The Necessity of Phase Transitions:** Water can't stay liquid forever. Seasons change, temperatures shift, and transformation becomes inevitable. Fighting phase transitions is futile; embracing them releases energy. The latent heat released when water freezes can warm the air around it. Every transition has hidden gifts.

**Underground Rivers:** Much of Earth's freshwater is invisible - aquifers, groundwater, moisture in soil. The most important water is often unseen. As we age, our visible accomplishments matter less than the invisible influence we've had - the conversations that changed minds, the support that enabled others, the values passed down.

**Erosion and Patience:** Water carved the Grand Canyon not through force but through persistence over millions of years. Sometimes the most powerful thing is gentle, consistent presence. The river doesn't fight the rock; it outlasts it.

**The Source and the Ocean:** Every river flows from a source to a destination, gathering tributaries along the way. Our lives follow similar paths - from individual beginnings, through connections with others, toward something larger than ourselves. We don't lose ourselves by joining the ocean; we become part of something infinite.
keyPoints: Water maintains identity while constantly transforming
Adapting to circumstances is intelligence, not weakness
Phase transitions are inevitable and release hidden energy
Invisible influence often matters more than visible achievement
Persistence over time accomplishes what force cannot
interactionPrompts: What phase of water do you feel like right now in life?
What 'invisible rivers' have shaped who you've become?
What has gentle persistence accomplished that force could not?
en.wisdomMoment: We are 60% water, and we cycle like water. The children we raise will carry our influence forward like rivers carrying water to the sea. We evaporate, condense, flow, freeze, and melt - but we never disappear. We transform.
en.core_metaphor: Life flows like water - changing form while maintaining essence
en.cta: The next time you drink water, consider: this same water has witnessed billions of years of change. What wisdom might it hold?
en.summary: You've explored the philosophical parallels between water's eternal cycling and the transformations of human life - finding wisdom in adaptation, patience, and invisible influence.

es.title: Sabiduría del Agua: Ciclos de Cambio
es.welcome: Estamos en una etapa de la vida donde hemos visto ciclos - carreras, relaciones, estaciones. El agua ha estado ciclando por 4.5 mil millones de años, enseñando una clase magistral en transformación sin pérdida de esencia.
es.mainContent:
**La Paradoja de la Constancia:** Las moléculas de agua en tu cuerpo fueron una vez lluvia sobre dinosaurios. El agua nunca se pierde - solo cambia de forma. La identidad no requiere estasis.

**Adaptarse a los Contenedores:** El agua líquida toma la forma de lo que la contiene. Adaptarse a las circunstancias no es debilidad - es inteligencia.

**La Necesidad de Transiciones:** El agua no puede permanecer líquida para siempre. Abrazar las transiciones libera energía.

**Ríos Subterráneos:** Gran parte del agua dulce es invisible. Nuestra influencia invisible a menudo importa más que los logros visibles.

**Erosión y Paciencia:** El agua talló el Gran Cañón no por fuerza sino por persistencia.
keyPoints: El agua mantiene identidad mientras se transforma
Adaptarse es inteligencia, no debilidad
Las transiciones liberan energía oculta
La influencia invisible importa más que los logros visibles

es.wisdomMoment: Somos 60% agua, y ciclamos como el agua. Nos evaporamos, condensamos, fluimos - pero nunca desaparecemos. Nos transformamos.
es.core_metaphor: La vida fluye como el agua - cambiando forma mientras mantiene esencia

61-102.title: Water: The Eternal Witness
61-102.description: Reflecting on water's timeless presence through a lifetime

en.title: Water: The Eternal Witness
en.welcome: You've witnessed perhaps 25,000 sunrises. The water in your morning cup has witnessed 4.5 billion. It was here before any life existed and will remain long after. Today, let's sit with this ancient companion and consider what it's seen - and what it reflects back to us.
en.mainContent:
**The Same Water, Different Vessels:** The water you drank as a child is the same water - the same actual molecules - cycling through Earth for billions of years. You have been many vessels for this ancient traveler. The baby, the student, the worker, the parent, the elder - different shapes, same water passing through. You've been like water yourself: many forms, one continuous existence.

**First Rain, Last Rain:** Somewhere on Earth right now, a child is experiencing their first rainstorm with wonder. Somewhere else, someone is watching rain through a window, knowing it may be among their last. The rain doesn't change. Our relationship to it deepens. What seemed ordinary becomes precious. Water taught us this: presence itself is the gift.

**The Ocean Returns:** Rivers don't end - they return to the ocean. The water that fell on your childhood home, that you swam in, that witnessed your wedding, that cooled your children's fevers - it all returns to the great reservoir, carrying traces of every moment. Nothing is truly lost.

**Ice Cores and Memory:** Scientists drill into Antarctic ice to read Earth's climate history. Each layer is frozen time - atmospheric composition, temperature, volcanic activity captured in ice. Your memory is like those ice cores: layers of experience, frozen moments you can touch again. Water holds memory. So do you.

**The Final Transformation:** Our bodies are water's temporary home. When we release these forms, the water continues its journey - back to clouds, to rain, to rivers, to oceans, perhaps to future life. We don't die - we transform, like water has always taught us. We become part of the cycle.

**A Glass of Water, A Universe:** Holding a glass of water, you hold the universe in miniature. Hydrogen from the Big Bang. Oxygen forged in stars. Molecules that passed through countless living things. This simple act - drinking water - connects you to cosmic history and future possibility.
keyPoints: The same water molecules have cycled through your entire life
What seemed ordinary becomes precious with time
Nothing is truly lost - it returns to the cycle
Memory, like ice cores, preserves experience in layers
We are temporary vessels; water is eternal

en.wisdomMoment: The water in your cells has witnessed creation itself. When you drink, you commune with eternity. When you return your water to the cycle, you give a gift to future generations. We are water's way of experiencing itself - briefly individual, eternally part of the flow.
en.core_metaphor: We are water's temporary vessels, passing along an eternal gift

es.title: El Agua: La Testigo Eterna
es.welcome: Has presenciado quizás 25,000 amaneceres. El agua en tu taza de la mañana ha presenciado 4.5 mil millones. Estuvo aquí antes de que existiera cualquier vida y permanecerá mucho después.
es.mainContent:
**La Misma Agua, Diferentes Vasijas:** El agua que bebiste de niño es la misma agua - las mismas moléculas - ciclando por la Tierra durante miles de millones de años. Has sido como el agua: muchas formas, una existencia continua.

**Primera Lluvia, Última Lluvia:** En algún lugar ahora, un niño experimenta su primera tormenta. En otro lugar, alguien mira la lluvia sabiendo que puede ser de las últimas. La lluvia no cambia. Nuestra relación con ella se profundiza.

**El Océano Regresa:** Los ríos no terminan - regresan al océano. Nada se pierde verdaderamente.

**Núcleos de Hielo y Memoria:** Tu memoria es como esos núcleos de hielo: capas de experiencia, momentos congelados que puedes tocar de nuevo.

**La Transformación Final:** Nuestros cuerpos son el hogar temporal del agua. Cuando liberamos estas formas, el agua continúa su viaje.

fr.title: L'Eau: Le Témoin Éternel
fr.welcome: Tu as peut-être vu 25 000 levers de soleil. L'eau dans ta tasse du matin en a vu 4,5 milliards. Elle était là avant toute vie et restera longtemps après.
fr.mainContent:
**La Même Eau, Différents Récipients:** L'eau que tu as bue enfant est la même eau - les mêmes molécules - cyclant à travers la Terre depuis des milliards d'années. Tu as été comme l'eau: beaucoup de formes, une existence continue.

**Première Pluie, Dernière Pluie:** Quelque part maintenant, un enfant vit sa première tempête. Ailleurs, quelqu'un regarde la pluie sachant que c'est peut-être parmi les dernières. La pluie ne change pas. Notre relation avec elle s'approfondit.

**L'Océan Revient:** Les rivières ne finissent pas - elles retournent à l'océan. Rien n'est vraiment perdu.

**Carottes de Glace et Mémoire:** Ta mémoire est comme ces carottes de glace: des couches d'expérience, des moments gelés que tu peux toucher à nouveau.

**La Transformation Finale:** Nos corps sont la maison temporaire de l'eau. Quand nous libérons ces formes, l'eau continue son voyage.

interactions.question: What do you think happens to water when it gets really cold?

choices.response: Exactly right! Water turns solid when it gets cold enough. Let's discover why!
Water never really disappears - it just changes form! Let me show you how.
That's a great starting point! Learning means discovering new things together.

2-5.question: What happens when you put water in the freezer?

choices.response: Yes! It becomes ICE! Water does a magic trick in the freezer!
That's right! Ice cubes are frozen water! Let's learn about water's magic!
Let's find out together! Water can do amazing things!

61-102.question: When you think of water, what memories come to mind?

choices.text: Swimming and playing as a child
choices.response: Those waters still carry echoes of joy. Water holds our memories as it cycles through time.
The rain that fell then has since traveled the world, carrying those moments forward.

choices.text: The simple pleasure of drinking water
choices.response: A simple act connecting us to billions of years of cycling. Let's reflect on this ancient companion.

interactions.question: Water can be solid (ice), liquid (water), and gas (steam). Which form do you think moves the fastest?

choices.response: Perfect! Gas molecules zoom around with the most energy. They've broken free!
Good thinking! Liquid molecules do slide around, but gas molecules move even faster - they're flying free!
Actually, ice molecules barely move at all - they're locked in place! Gas molecules have the most energy and zoom around.

2-5.question: Can you make a splash with ice or with water?

choices.response: Yes! Water goes splash splash! Ice is too hard to splash!
That's right! Ice is solid and hard. Water is wet and splashy!

interactions.question: The Sun heats ocean water. What happens next in the water cycle?

choices.response: Exactly! The Sun's energy transforms liquid water into invisible vapor that rises into the sky.
Water does warm up, and when it gets enough energy, it evaporates! It rises up as invisible gas.
Actually, warm water rises! And when the Sun heats it enough, it evaporates into the air as invisible water vapor.

2-5.question: Where do puddles go when the Sun comes out?

choices.response: Yes! The Sun makes puddles float away into the sky! That's water's magic!
Some water does go into the ground! But most floats up to the sky when the Sun warms it!

interactions.question: What's the most amazing thing about water's ability to transform?

choices.text: It never runs out - it just keeps cycling
choices.response: That's the magic! The same water has been cycling for billions of years. It's eternal.

choices.text: It can become solid, liquid, or gas
choices.response: Yes! Water is a master of transformation. It adapts to whatever temperature it encounters.
Beautiful insight! Every living thing shares the same water. We're all connected by this flowing molecule.

2-5.question: What's your favorite way water can be?

choices.response: Yummy! Ice cream is frozen and cold - just like how water becomes ice!
Splash splash! Bath water is wet and fun - that's liquid water!
Clouds are made of tiny water drops! Water floated all the way up to make those fluffy shapes!

61-102.question: What wisdom does water's eternal cycling offer you?

choices.response: A profound truth. Water transforms but never disappears. Neither do we, in the ways that matter most.
Water teaches this beautifully. Staying frozen isn't living; flowing is. Each transition has its purpose.

choices.text: We are all connected through time
choices.response: The water in you has touched countless lives across billions of years. We are part of one great flow.
